newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes easier in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes easier in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar slid to a lower close against the U.S. dollar on Thursday in a series of book-squaring trades before the long holiday weekend.
The rate ended at T$27.480 versus T$27.470 at Wednesday's close. A total of US$280.5 million changed hands, making it the busiest trading day of the holiday-shortened week.

The U.S. dollar had been under weather since the Federal Reserve Board decided to keep the key interest rates unchanged on late Tueday after the market closed in Taiwan . But it embarked on a robust recovery despite lingering doubts about the inflationary scenario in the U.S.
"The U.S. dollar turned out to be quite resilient," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The broadly based bounce of the U.S. dollar made dealers reluctant to hold positions over the long weekend, he said.
The financial markets will be closed on Friday for the Mid-autumn festival and on Saturday for Confucius Day.
The markets will reopen on Monday.
